impl_requirements: Emit a single .cu/.hip translation unit, OR (when --build-cmd is supplied) modify an in-codebase kernel and rely on the project build system. For standalone mode: expose a PYBIND11_MODULE with a forward() binding; hipcc compiles to .so. For in-codebase mode: the build command is run verbatim.
read_metric_guide: High dram_pct with low sm_pct => DDR/HBM bandwidth bound (typical for APU with shared DDR5). High sm_pct with low dram_pct => compute_bound. Low occupancy with neither saturated => latency_occupancy. Many short kernels / launch-dominated wall time => overhead_bound. On RDNA, wave32 vs wave64 choice and LDS bank conflicts (32 banks 4B wide) are common levers.

vectorized_load_store.prompt_guidance: Widen memory transactions to 128-bit so each thread moves 16 bytes per access; on RDNA wave32 this matches one DDR/HBM burst window (32 lanes * 16 B = 512 B).

memory_coalescing.prompt_guidance: Reorder the thread-to-element mapping so consecutive threads in a wave read consecutive addresses; wave32 on RDNA, wave64 on CDNA.

shared_memory_tiling.prompt_guidance: Stage reused operands into LDS per block, sync, then compute from LDS to cut redundant DDR/HBM traffic. RDNA LDS is 64KB/CU with 32 banks 4B wide; pad inner strides so gcd(stride,32)==1 to avoid bank conflicts.

async_copy_pipeline.prompt_guidance: Overlap the next tile's global->LDS copy with the current tile's compute. On gfx11 use global_load_lds; on CDNA use buffer_load_dword_lds.

l2_cache_reuse.idiom: GQA-batched / wave-grouped reads so L1/L2 serves repeats
l2_cache_reuse.prompt_guidance: When multiple Q heads share a KV head (GQA), arrange the schedule so consecutive Q reads of the same K/V token hit L1 (16KB/CU on RDNA) instead of going back to DDR.

tensor_core_mma.prompt_guidance: Use __builtin_amdgcn_mfma_* on CDNA, __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_* on RDNA3+ for the inner GEMM with fp16/bf16 operands. On RDNA3.5 also use v_dot2_f32_f16 for 2-element half2 dot products.

instruction_reduction.idiom: strength reduction and loop unrolling (#pragma unroll)
instruction_reduction.prompt_guidance: Hoist invariants, replace divides/mods with shifts where legal, and #pragma unroll the inner loop to cut issued VALU instructions.

fast_math_intrinsics.prompt_guidance: Where precision tolerance allows, replace transcendental calls with __-prefixed device intrinsics.

register_tiling.prompt_guidance: Accumulate an MxN micro-tile in VGPRs (RDNA) or AGPRs (CDNA MFMA) per thread to raise arithmetic intensity. Budget against 256 VGPR/wave for 8 waves/SIMD on RDNA.

occupancy_increase.prompt_guidance: Annotate the kernel with __launch_bounds__(N, max_waves_per_simd) and shrink live state. RDNA target: 8 waves/SIMD at 256 VGPRs/wave (32 VGPRs/thread).

block_size_tuning.prompt_guidance: On RDNA, block sizes that are multiples of 32 (wave32) keep the SIMDs balanced; 128 or 256 is the usual sweet spot. On CDNA prefer multiples of 64.

register_pressure_reduction.prompt_guidance: Shorten variable lifetimes and prefer recompute over caching to keep VGPR count below the spill-to-scratch threshold.

launch_config_tuning.idiom: grid/block geometry and dynamic LDS sizing
launch_config_tuning.prompt_guidance: Tune gridDim/blockDim and dynamic LDS bytes so the launch geometry matches the CU count and tile shape.

kernel_fusion.idiom: fuse the elementwise epilogue into the main kernel
kernel_fusion.prompt_guidance: Avoid a second launch by computing the elementwise epilogue inside the producing kernel before the store.

launch_overhead_reduction.prompt_guidance: Collapse many tiny launches into a persistent kernel or a captured HIP graph to amortize launch cost.

library_fallback_hybrid.idiom: delegate the hot GEMM to rocBLAS / hipBLASLt
library_fallback_hybrid.prompt_guidance: When a vendor library kernel dominates, call rocBLAS / hipBLASLt / MIOpen for the heavy op and keep custom code only for the glue.

cpu_gpu_overlap.prompt_guidance: Split the work across HIP streams so host<->device copies overlap kernel execution. On an APU with unified memory this is typically a no-op.
